cosmetics.title: Egyptian Cosmetics Analytics
cosmetics.intro: An Egypt-focused retail portfolio project connecting operational data to a dimensional warehouse and Power BI reporting.
cosmetics.problem: An omnichannel retail scenario brings together orders, customer records, inventory, targets, and exchange-rate inputs. Mixed formats and inconsistent values need a clear treatment before they can support reporting.
approach: Ingest CSV, Excel, and JSON inputs with Python and preserve raw records with lineage.
Standardize fields, validate relationships, and route invalid records into explicit quarantine tables.
Model dimensions and facts in SQL Server, including customer history with SCD Type 2.
Provide SQL Server and Power Query delivery paths with a DAX semantic layer.
cosmetics.takeaway: The useful part is the complete chain: a source record can be traced through cleaning, validation, modeling, and reporting. The repository documents the scenario, architecture, and data-quality decisions.
cosmetics.caveat: Portfolio business scenario. Do not interpret the company narrative or sample data as a real client engagement, verified market performance, or measured business impact. The cover graphic is an illustration.
cosmetics.stack: Python · SQL Server 2022 · Power Query M · Power BI · DAX

pixelfed.title: PixelFed, from raw to ready
pixelfed.intro: A reproducible social-content analytics project built around a relational schema, mixed-format landing files, and a galaxy semantic model.
pixelfed.problem: Social-content data has different event grains, optional values, and timing constraints. Landing data also arrives in different file formats. Cleaning everything with the same rule can quietly change its meaning.
approach: Generate deterministic synthetic data against a documented schema contract.
Separate natural optional nulls from deliberately injected raw-data quality issues.
Validate a candidate landing refresh before explicit promotion and retain the prior snapshot.
Use Power Query staging and conformed dimensions with grain-specific facts and documented relationships.
pixelfed.takeaway: The project makes the raw-to-Silver workflow reviewable: schemas, null-handling policies, validation, and manual Power Query guidance sit alongside the implementation.
pixelfed.caveat: All accounts, names, posts, and events are synthetic. Dated Egypt-market references inform the scenario; they do not establish real PixelFed audience sizes or business results. This is social-content analytics, not a sales dataset.
pixelfed.stack: Python · Power Query M · Power BI · TMDL · SQL · GitHub Actions

kickstarter.title: Making sense of Kickstarter
kickstarter.intro: A Power BI analytics-engineering project designed to reconcile campaign history across public Kickstarter data sources.
kickstarter.problem: Historical dumps and recurring crawls overlap. A campaign can appear repeatedly with changing states, while regional benchmarks exist at a different grain. Appending everything into a single flat table can inflate results.
approach: Stage sources independently and normalize encoding, naming, types, and dates.
Apply documented source hierarchy and recency rules to deduplicate campaign records.
Separate campaign outcomes, campaign snapshots, and regional benchmarks in a galaxy model.
Keep the semantic model reviewable in Git using PBIP and TMDL, with organized DAX measures.
kickstarter.takeaway: The model treats grain as an explicit design decision. Campaign outcomes and time-series snapshots can answer different questions without being mixed into a misleading total.
kickstarter.caveat: The underlying files are historical public snapshots from sources including Kaggle and WebRobots. Overlapping raw observations are not a count of unique campaigns. The project cover is conceptual, not a live report.
kickstarter.stack: Power Query M · Power BI · DAX · PBIP · TMDL · Python

n8n.title: Automation with a backbone
n8n.intro: A documented Docker Compose stack for queue-mode n8n workflows, with Redis, PostgreSQL, and worker-oriented execution.
n8n.problem: A useful automation setup needs care around execution, persistence, scaling, recovery, and upgrades. Connecting a few workflow nodes is only one part of the system.
approach: Separate workflow editing, webhook handling, and queued worker execution.
Use Redis for the queue and PostgreSQL for workflow and execution persistence.
Include worker-scaling logic, runner configuration, monitoring, and dependency health checks.
Document backups, operations, troubleshooting, and upgrade or rollback procedures.
n8n.takeaway: The repository combines workflow examples with the infrastructure and runbooks around them. It reflects my interest in systems that can be understood, repeated, and maintained.
n8n.caveat: This is a self-hosted portfolio setup. Repository features are not a claim of production uptime, benchmarked throughput, or client deployments. Version-specific setup and migration guidance lives in the repository.
n8n.stack: n8n · Docker Compose · Python · Redis · PostgreSQL · Qdrant
